unit.why: A narrative, quoted from Yitav Panim, about R. Moshe Teitelbaum, then exploring Hasidism. He silently prayed that the Seer of Lublin would resolve his doubt about constant Hasidic joy versus mourning for the Temple, and the Seer answered it unasked as soon as he arrived.

stories.start_quote: בספר ייט״פ להגאוה״ק בעל ייט"ל הנ"ל
stories.summary_en: R. Moshe Teitelbaum, while investigating the ways of the Hasidim, doubted their constant joy given the halakhic duty to mourn the Temple. He prayed that the Seer of Lublin would resolve this, and on arrival the Seer answered him unprompted with a parable from R. Shmelke of Nikolsburg about a captive king lodging with a friend.
